name: bare-assert
usage:
```js
const assert = require('bare-assert')

assert(1 + 1 === 2, 'sum should be correct')

assert.equal(1, 1)
assert.notEqual(1, 2)
```

members.name: assert.deepStrictEqual
signatures: assert.deepStrictEqual(actual: any, expected: any, message?: string | Error): void
members.description:
Throw an `AssertionError` unless `actual` and `expected` are the same value recursively. A pair
that is not two objects is compared with `Object.is()`, which treats `NaN` as equal to `NaN`
and `0` as distinct from `-0`. Two objects must share a prototype, and are then compared by
their own enumerable properties, descending into the values reachable from them. Boxed
primitives, dates, regular expressions, errors, buffers, typed arrays, maps, and sets are each
compared by what they hold; weak maps, weak sets, and promises are compared by reference.
Cycles are handled.

params.name: actual
params.description: The value produced.

params.name: expected
params.description: The value to compare `actual` against.

params.name: message
params.description:
Custom message for the thrown error; if an `Error` instance, it is thrown
directly instead of an `AssertionError`.

throws.condition:
thrown if the values are not recursively equal (unless `message` is an
`Error` instance, which is thrown instead).

members.name: assert.doesNotMatch
signatures: assert.doesNotMatch(actual: string, expected: RegExp, message?: string | Error): void
members.description:
Throw an `AssertionError` unless `actual` is a string that does not match the `expected`

params.name: actual

params.name: message
params.description:

directly instead of an `AssertionError`.

throws.condition:
thrown if `actual` is not a string or matches `expected` (unless
`message` is an `Error` instance, which is thrown instead).

members.name: assert.doesNotReject
signatures: assert.doesNotReject(fn: (() => Promise<unknown>) | Promise<unknown>, message?: string | Error): Promise<void>
assert.doesNotReject(fn: (() => Promise<unknown>) | Promise<unknown>, error: ((err: unknown) => boolean) | RegExp | Error | object, message?: string | Error): Promise<void>
members.description:
Reject with an `AssertionError` if `fn` rejects. The returned promise settles once the
assertion has been made, so it must be awaited.

params.name: fn
params.description:
The promise to await, or a function returning one; a function that throws
synchronously propagates rather than counting as a rejection.

params.name: message
params.description:
Custom message for the error; if an `Error` instance, it is used directly
instead of an `AssertionError`.

returns.description:
A promise that resolves once the assertion has passed, and rejects with an
`AssertionError` if `fn` rejects (or with `message` if it is an `Error` instance).

exports.name: AssertionError
signatures: AssertionError
exports.description:
Error thrown when an assertion fails, carrying the `actual`, `expected`, and `operator`
involved.

members.name: AssertionError

params.name: opts
params.type: { message?: string; actual?: any; expected?: any; operator?: string }

members.name: actual
signatures: actual: any
members.description: The actual value that failed the assertion.

members.name: expected
signatures: expected: any
members.description: The expected value the assertion was checked against.

members.name: operator

members.description:
The comparison operator used by the assertion that failed, for example `'=='` or
`'strictEqual'`.
